title: TypeScript
description: Type-safe JavaScript — types, generics, classes and modern tooling.

chapters.title: Types on Top of JavaScript
objectives: Explain the core ideas behind tsc and annotations.

exercises.question: What is the purpose of tsc in TypeScript?
exercises.answer: tsc lets you tsconfig — see chapter section 1.2.

exercises.question: Modify the example to keep three decimal places instead of two.
exercises.answer: Format the printed value with the language's precision formatter (e.g. printf/round), then re-run and compare.

exercises.question: When would you avoid tsconfig?
exercises.answer: Avoid it when the task is better served by a simpler, linear approach — momentum matters more than cleverness.

tests.instructions: One assessment per chapter grouping plus a final exam. Every question maps to the section shown in brackets so you can revise precisely.

questions.q: Which concept makes tsc behave that way? (TypeScript ch.1)
The worked sample prints "Compiles; typos fail at build time". Which statement caused it? (ch.1)
Which concept makes interface behave that way? (TypeScript ch.2)
The worked sample prints "data is only accessible when ok === true". Which statement caused it? (ch.2)
Which concept makes tuple behave that way? (TypeScript ch.3)
The worked sample prints "New type with only those two fields". Which statement caused it? (ch.3)
Which concept makes public/private behave that way? (TypeScript ch.4)
The worked sample prints "Compiler enforces total() exists". Which statement caused it? (ch.4)
Which concept makes T behave that way? (TypeScript ch.5)
The worked sample prints "wrap(3) → number[]". Which statement caused it? (ch.5)
Which concept makes import type behave that way? (TypeScript ch.6)
The worked sample prints "Type-only import erased at runtime". Which statement caused it? (ch.6)
Which concept makes vite behave that way? (TypeScript ch.7)
The worked sample prints "Test passes with full type inference". Which statement caused it? (ch.7)

assessment.q: Write TypeScript code that reads a value, transforms it and prints the result. (final)
What does the score of 14.3 marks per chapter tell you about this exam's structure? (final)
